title: CVE-2024-2466: TLS certificate check bypass with mbedTLS
excerpt:
## Summary:

Curl library has a security vulnerability where the certificate name check is bypassed when connecting to a host via its IP address. This could potentially introduce spoofing attacks or unauthorized access due to unverified server certificate.

This issue only affects the Curl with MbedTLS.

- Affected versions: from libcurl 8.5.0 to and including 8.6.0 (current master versions at the time of writing)
- Not affected versions: libcurl 8.4.0 and earlier

This issue affect all kinds of protocol over TLS session, e.g. HTTPS, FTPS, SMTPS, etc.

## Steps To Reproduce:

### (Preparation) Download and build the Curl with MbedTLS:

*Skip this step if you already have the Curl (>= 8.5.0) with MbedTLS.*

Before building the code, make sure you have environment to build the code in Linux, `sudo apt install build-essential`.

1. Get and extract the code:

```shell
wget https://curl.se/download/curl-8.6.0.tar.gz -O curl-8.6.0.tar.gz
wget https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.7.tar.gz -O mbedtls-2.28.7.tar.gz
tar zxf curl-8.6.0.tar.gz
tar zxf mbedtls-2.28.7.tar.gz
```

2. Build MbedTLS:

```shell
cd mbedtls-2.28.7
make SHARED=1 -j$(nproc)
sudo make install DESTDIR=/usr/local/lib
```

3. Build Curl with MbedTLS:

```shell
cd curl-8.6.0
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib
export PATH=/usr/local/lib:$PATH
./configure --with-mbedtls=/usr/local --without-libpsl
make -j$(nproc) CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include" LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"
```

### Reproduce the issue via Curl CLI:

If you build the Curl with MbedTLS from above, you should export the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `PATH` to use the built Curl.

```shell
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib
export PATH=/usr/local/lib:$PATH
```

1. Check the version of the Curl:

```shell
$ curl --version
curl 8.6.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.6.0 mbedTLS/2.28.7 zlib/1.2.11 libidn2/2.2.0
Release-Date: 2024-01-31
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps ipfs ipns mqtt pop3 pop3s rtsp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp
Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS HSTS HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Largefile libz NTLM SSL threadsafe UnixSockets
```

2. Get IP from an example https server and use it to connect:

```shell
$ host -t A www.example.org
www.example.org has address 93.184.216.34
$ curl https://93.184.216.34
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?>
<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Trans

summary: Curl library bypasses TLS certificate name check when connecting via IP address, allowing spoofing attacks.

claims.text: mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname is not called when SNI is not set, causing server certificate name verification to be bypassed
claims.reasoning: Curl_ssl_peer_init only sets peer->sni for DNS hostnames (not IP addresses). The report states mbed_connect_step1 only calls mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname when peer->sni is set. External mbedTLS documentation confirms mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname is required for CN/SAN verification regardless of SNI usage. The deterministic checks confirm the symbols exist and the core quoted lines appear in the codebase.

citations.note: peer->sni = calloc(...) only for DNS names
mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname() must be called for server name verification even when SNI is not used, as it also sets the name for CN/SAN checks

claims.reasoning: The function mbed_connect_step1 exists in lib/vtls/mbedtls.c at the expected location per deterministic checks.

citations.note: grounded symbol: mbed_connect_step1 exists in curl

claims.text: connecting to a host by its IP address instead of its DNS name
claims.reasoning: The peer type enum values for IP addresses exist and are used in get_peer_type to classify IP hostnames, which then prevents sni from being set.

citations.note: grounded symbols: CURL_SSL_PEER_IPV4 and CURL_SSL_PEER_IPV6 exist in curl

claims.text: SSL handshake completes without verifying the server's certificate against the host name, enabling spoofing
claims.reasoning: External sources confirm that skipping mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname bypasses CN/SAN verification, enabling spoofing/impersonation attacks with valid certificates for different domains.

citations.note: if a TLS client application does not call mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname(), the first step is silently skipped. This allows any server with a certificate signed by a trusted CA to impersonate any other server

If the certificate's host-specific data is not properly checked... it may be possible for a redirection or spoofing attack to allow a malicious host with a valid certificate to provide data, impersonating a trusted host

key_reasons: Curl_ssl_peer_init only sets peer->sni for DNS hostnames (lines 1589-1603 in lib/vtls/vtls.c), leaving it NULL for IP addresses
mbed_connect_step1 (per report and grounded symbols) only calls mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname when peer->sni is set
mbedTLS documentation explicitly states mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname is required for CN/SAN verification even without SNI
This bypasses server certificate host verification, enabling spoofing with valid certificates for other domains (CWE-297)
The bug was previously fixed for CVE-2016-3739 but reintroduced by later refactoring per the commit history analysis
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction steps. The issue is confirmed: when connecting via IP address, peer->sni is not set (lib/vtls/vtls.c:1589-1603), so mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname is not called in mbed_connect_step1, bypassing CN/SAN verification. mbedTLS documentation confirms this function must be called for host verification regardless of SNI usage. This reintroduces CVE-2016-3739. We will fix by calling mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname with peer->hostname even when sni is NULL.
